title: The carousel bug hiding behind one boolean
excerpt: Two independent reasons to pause an autoplaying carousel were sharing a single piece of state. The result looked fine until you moved your mouse in a specific order.
content:
I was porting a testimonial carousel between two projects and found a bug that had been sitting in the original the whole time. It came down to one `useState`.

## The setup

An autoplaying deck should hold still for two different reasons: the pointer is over it, or something inside it has keyboard focus. Both are "pause" — so both wrote to the same flag.

```jsx
const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);

<div
  onMouseEnter={() => setPaused(true)}
  onMouseLeave={() => setPaused(false)}
  onFocusCapture={() => setPaused(true)}
  onBlurCapture={() => setPaused(false)}
>
```

Read each handler on its own and every one is correct. Read them together and there's a hole.

## The hole

Hover the deck, tab to a dot, then tab away. `onBlurCapture` fires and sets `paused` to `false` — while your cursor is still sitting on the deck. Autoplay resumes and the cards start sliding under your mouse, which is precisely the thing hover-pause exists to prevent.

The reverse works too. Focus something inside, move the mouse off, and `onMouseLeave` clears the pause even though focus is still inside.

It's a lost-update problem. Two independent producers, one slot, last writer wins.

## The fix

Track the reasons separately and derive the answer:

```jsx
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false);
const [focused, setFocused] = useState(false);
const [tabHidden, setTabHidden] = useState(false);

const paused = hovered || focused || tabHidden;
```

Now each handler owns exactly one fact and can't clobber another. `paused` isn't state at all — it's a question you ask about state, so it can't drift out of sync.

## Why testing it was harder than fixing it

My first attempt to reproduce it in a browser gave three misleading results in a row, and every one was my measurement rather than the code.

**`mouseenter` doesn't fire on a reload.** If the cursor already sits inside the element when the page loads, no boundary is crossed, so no `mouseenter`. `mouseover` fires repeatedly, `mouseenter` never does. I had to move the pointer away and back to get a real crossing.

**`.focus()` scrolls.** Focusing an element scrolls it into view, which moved the deck out from under the cursor and fired a genuine `mouseleave` — so the resume I "caught" was caused by my own test. `focus({ preventScroll: true })` fixed that.

**Freezing CSS doesn't freeze JavaScript.** I injected `* { animation: none !important; transition: none !important }` for a stable screenshot, then read a counter that was mid-animation anyway, because it was driven by `requestAnimationFrame`, not CSS. It reported 30 when the real value was 31.

The lesson that stuck: when a browser test disagrees with your reading of the code, suspect the test first. All three of those failures looked exactly like product bugs.

## The smell, generalised

If you find yourself writing `setThing(true)` from more than one unrelated event, that boolean is probably several booleans wearing a trenchcoat. Derived state is free; synchronised state is a maintenance bill.
author: Leomar Abad
